title: An Efficient Bit-level Sparse MAC-accelerated Architecture with SW/HW Co-design on FPGA
problem: Bit-level sparsity exploitation for MAC units is a proven efficiency improvement, but FPGA implementations face architectural limitations; existing FPGA designs lack effective bit-level sparsity support compared to ASIC value-aware accelerators.
motivation: FPGAs offer reconfigurability and shorter time-to-market for neural network accelerators, but bit-level sparsity optimization remains underexplored on FPGAs compared to ASICs.
method: The solution combines software and hardware design: the software creates an encoding (a way of representing numbers and data) tailored to work with FPGA lookup tables—the small memory blocks FPGAs use to implement logic—with adjustable sensitivity to detect zero bits. The hardware handles multiply-accumulate operations that take variable time depending on sparsity. This allows FPGAs to efficiently skip computing with zero bits while keeping results accurate.
key_novelty: An encoding scheme designed for FPGA lookup tables with adjustable granularity to detect and exploit bit-level sparsity in multiply-accumulate operations while maintaining accuracy and timing closure.
contributions: LUT-friendly encoding with adaptable granularity for bit-level sparsity on FPGAs
Hardware structure supporting multiplication time uncertainty for variable-latency operations
Improved trade-off between redundancy exploitation and accuracy preservation
Processing elements 2.2x smaller than bit-parallel designs; 1.04-1.74x performance boost vs bit-parallel, 1.40-2.79x vs Booth-based designs
limitations: Abstract does not discuss memory bandwidth requirements, comparison with ASIC implementations, or scalability to larger neural networks.
primary_theme: LUT-friendly bit-sparse MAC accelerator on FPGA
